messages:
ida: quick RFC follow-up: propose we unalias the "shared-enricher" library into two explicit services: enrich-core (hotpath) and enrich-batch (offline). goal: shrink hot-path surface area, reduce deploy blast radius, and make ownership clear. thoughts?
sam: makes sense. question: how do we route existing callers? do we maintain a facade proxy for a migration window? :thinking: 
oliver: prefer a phased migration with a compatibility facade. facade can route by feature-flag per-tenant and translate calls to new endpoints. keep it thin.
priya: ops checklist idea: 1) publish new services behind internal DNS 2) add facade with dual-write/dual-read toggles 3) run backfill parity for 50k events 4) ramp cohorts by traffic tier. also add a 2-week deprecation window for the old lib.
ida: agree. also propose a conservation rule: any enrichment moved to enrich-batch must have bounded memory & CPU so it never affects hotpath tail.
sam: monitoring: track enrich-latency-p99, enrichment-coverage, and facet-drift. add an alert if parity drift > 0.3% during canary.
priya: add trace-id propagation and tag changes so SRE can correlate spans across facade -> new svc. otherwise debugging will be painful.
oliver: ownership: product team owns data model; eng-runtime owns operational SLO for enrich-core. capture infra cost allocation before rollout.
ida: rollback: keep facade defaulting to old lib until post-cutover freeze. plan a kill-switch flag to route all traffic back.
infra-bot: rollout pipeline: "enrich-split-v1" staged to staging at 2025-11-02T09:12Z. backfill job scaffolded.
sam: small ask: standardize RPC contract (http+json) and include versioned schema to avoid subtle mismatches.
ida: will add schema v1 and an adapter for legacy callers. I'll update the RFC with phased gates and checklist. please react with :thumbsup: if you approve.
